title: Triangles
prerequisites: Properties of parallel lines and a transversal.
Area of a triangle as ½ × base × height.

topics.title: Similar Triangles and Criteria for Similarity
topics.quick_summary: Two triangles are similar if their corresponding angles are equal and corresponding sides are proportional, established by the AAA, SSS or SAS similarity criteria.
topics.real_life: The height of a tree is found by comparing its shadow with that of a metre stick — two similar triangles doing the measurement for you.

detailed.definition: Two triangles are similar if their corresponding angles are equal and their corresponding sides are in the same ratio. Congruent triangles are a special case of similar triangles with ratio 1.
detailed.key_idea: For triangles, equal angles automatically force proportional sides and vice versa. This is peculiar to triangles — for quadrilaterals both conditions must be checked separately.
detailed.working_principle: The AA criterion is enough because the third angle is then determined by the angle sum property. In practice AA is the criterion used in almost every problem.
applications: Basic Proportionality Theorem (Thales): a line parallel to one side divides the other two proportionally.
Its converse is used to prove that a line is parallel to a side.
The ratio of areas of two similar triangles equals the square of the ratio of corresponding sides.

points: Similarity criteria: AAA (or AA), SSS and SAS.
AA is sufficient because the third angle follows from the angle sum property.
Basic Proportionality Theorem: if DE ∥ BC then AD/DB = AE/EC.
Ratio of areas of similar triangles = (ratio of corresponding sides)².
All congruent triangles are similar, but similar triangles need not be congruent.
mistakes: Using SSA for similarity, which is not a valid criterion.
Taking the ratio of areas as the ratio of sides instead of its square.
Writing the correspondence of vertices in the wrong order.
topics.memory_hook: 'Same shape, different size' — angles equal, sides proportional, areas in the squared ratio.
topics.advanced: The squared area ratio generalises: for similar solids, volumes scale as the cube of the length ratio. This is why doubling every dimension of a model multiplies its weight by eight.

formulas.name: Basic Proportionality Theorem
formulas.formula: If DE ∥ BC, then AD/DB = AE/EC
formulas.variables: D and E are points on AB and AC of triangle ABC.
formulas.when_to_use: Whenever a line parallel to one side of a triangle cuts the other two sides.
formulas.common_mistakes: Pairing the segments incorrectly — AD must go with AE, and DB with EC.
formulas.shortcut: The converse proves parallelism from the proportion.

formulas.name: Ratio of Areas of Similar Triangles
formulas.variables: Corresponding sides of the two similar triangles.
formulas.when_to_use: To find an unknown area or side ratio between two similar triangles.
formulas.common_mistakes: Forgetting to square the side ratio.
formulas.shortcut: Sides in ratio 2:3 → areas in ratio 4:9.

topics.title: Pythagoras Theorem and Its Converse
topics.quick_summary: In a right triangle the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides, and the converse identifies right triangles from their side lengths.
topics.real_life: A mason checks a corner is square using the 3-4-5 rule — the converse of the Pythagoras theorem applied with a piece of string.

detailed.definition: Pythagoras theorem: in a right-angled triangle, the square of the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares of the other two sides. Its converse: if the square of one side equals the sum of the squares of the other two, the triangle is right-angled.
detailed.key_idea: The modern proof uses similar triangles: the altitude from the right angle to the hypotenuse creates two triangles each similar to the original. The theorem follows in three lines.
detailed.working_principle: The hypotenuse is always the longest side and lies opposite the right angle. Identifying it correctly before substituting is essential.
applications: The distance formula in coordinate geometry is the Pythagoras theorem.

points: In a right triangle: hypotenuse² = sum of squares of the other two sides.
The hypotenuse is opposite the right angle and is the longest side.
Converse: if c² = a² + b², the angle opposite c is a right angle.
If c² > a² + b² the triangle is obtuse; if c² < a² + b² it is acute.
The theorem is proved using similar triangles formed by the altitude to the hypotenuse.
mistakes: Treating any side as the hypotenuse instead of the longest one.
Applying the theorem to a triangle that is not right-angled.
Forgetting to take the square root at the end.
topics.memory_hook: 'Longest side squared equals the other two squared, added' — and 3-4-5 always works.
topics.advanced: The theorem generalises to the cosine rule c² = a² + b² − 2ab cos C, which reduces to Pythagoras when C = 90° and cos C = 0. Pythagoras is simply the right-angled special case.

formulas.name: Pythagoras Theorem
formulas.variables: hypotenuse = side opposite the right angle; the other two are the legs.
formulas.when_to_use: For any right-angled triangle, and in distance and diagonal calculations.
formulas.common_mistakes: Adding the squares of the hypotenuse and a leg.
formulas.shortcut: Recognise triples such as 3-4-5 and 5-12-13 to skip the arithmetic.
